## **ADR-030 — Docker Containerization & Container Image Architecture**

This should come next because the core application runtime stack is now established. We need to define **how Spring Boot, React-related server components, Gateway, AI services and supporting workloads become reproducible deployable artifacts before moving deeper into Kubernetes**.

ADR-030 should establish:

**Docker vs alternatives → OCI images → Dockerfile standards → Spring Boot multi-stage builds → Maven dependency caching → JAR layering → JRE vs JDK runtime images → Java 21 container awareness → React/Vite build containers → NGINX/static deployment boundary → AI/Python containers → base-image selection → Alpine vs Debian/distroless trade-offs → image pinning → digest pinning → multi-architecture images → non-root containers → read-only filesystem → Linux capabilities → secrets → environment configuration → `.dockerignore` → build context → image labels → SBOM → vulnerability scanning → Trivy → dependency scanning → image signing → provenance → Cosign/Sigstore direction → supply-chain security → reproducible builds → immutable images → tagging/version strategy → Git SHA → semantic versions → `latest` prohibition for production → registry strategy → Nexus/container registry relationship → image retention → Kubernetes resource compatibility → JVM memory/container limits → graceful shutdown → health checks → logs to stdout/stderr → temporary files → volumes → persistent-data prohibition for application containers → Docker Compose development environment → Testcontainers → CI builds → caching → BuildKit → build secrets → private Maven dependencies → image-size optimization → CVE patching → rebuild policy → emergency base-image updates → promotion across DEV/UAT/PROD → same-image promotion principle.**

# Architecture Decision Records (ADR)

---

---

# ADR-030 — Docker Containerization & Container Image Architecture

**Document Version:** 1.0
**ADR ID:** ADR-030
**Status:** Accepted
**Owner:** Enterprise Architecture Board (EAB)

Mediverse shall standardize application packaging and runtime delivery around **OCI-compatible container images**, using **Docker-compatible build workflows** and immutable-image promotion across environments.

The core principle is:

> **Build once, scan once, sign once, and promote the exact same immutable artifact through DEV → UAT → PROD.**

```text
Source Code
    │
    ▼
CI Build
    │
    ├── Compile/Test
    ├── Build OCI Image
    ├── Generate SBOM
    ├── Vulnerability Scan
    ├── Sign/Attest
    │
    ▼
Container Registry
    │
    ▼
DEV
    │
    ▼
UAT
    │
    ▼
PROD
```

Mediverse shall **not rebuild application images separately for each environment**.

---

## 1. Problem

Mediverse contains heterogeneous workloads:

```text
Spring Boot Microservices
Spring Cloud Gateway
React/Vite Frontend
Kafka Workers
Scheduled Jobs
AI/Python Services
Background Processing
Administrative Services
```

Without containerization standards, teams eventually produce incompatible deployment artifacts:

```text
Service A → java -jar manually

Service B → custom VM

Service C → Docker

Frontend → copied manually

AI service → Python virtualenv on server
```

This destroys deployment consistency.

---

# 2. Decision

Mediverse shall adopt:

```text
Docker-compatible builds
        +
OCI Container Images
        +
Container Registry
        +
Kubernetes Runtime
```

as the standard packaging architecture.

Application containers shall be:

* Immutable
* Reproducible
* Minimal
* Non-root where practical
* Environment-neutral
* Observable
* Scannable
* Versioned
* Signed where production supply-chain policy requires it

---

# 3. Docker vs OCI

Docker and OCI are related but not identical concepts.

```text
Docker
   │
   ├── Build tooling
   ├── Local development
   └── Container workflows

OCI
   │
   ├── Image specification
   └── Runtime specification
```

Mediverse architecture depends primarily on **OCI-compatible artifacts**, not permanently on one container-engine vendor.

---

# 4. Alternatives Considered

| Option                                    | Decision                           |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| OCI containers                            | ✅ Selected                         |
| Docker tooling                            | ✅ Primary developer/build workflow |
| Podman                                    | 🟡 Compatible alternative          |
| Buildpacks                                | 🟡 Selective future option         |
| Direct JAR deployment to servers          | ❌ Rejected                         |
| VM-per-service packaging                  | ❌ Rejected                         |
| Environment-specific application binaries | ❌ Rejected                         |

---

# 5. Containerization Boundary

Every independently deployable backend workload shall normally have its own container image.

```text
gateway-service
      │
      ▼
gateway image

content-service
      │
      ▼
content image

assessment-service
      │
      ▼
assessment image

ai-service
      │
      ▼
AI image
```

Do not create one giant image containing every Mediverse microservice.

---

# 6. One Process Per Container

The preferred model is:

```text
Container
   │
   └── Application Process
```

not:

```text
Container
   ├── Spring Boot
   ├── PostgreSQL
   ├── Redis
   ├── NGINX
   └── Cron
```

Containers should represent independently manageable workloads.

---

# 7. Spring Boot Image Architecture

A Spring Boot service should follow:

```text
Source
  │
  ▼
Maven Build
  │
  ▼
Executable JAR
  │
  ▼
Runtime Image
  │
  ▼
Kubernetes
```

---

# 8. Multi-Stage Builds

Production images shall use multi-stage builds where source compilation occurs inside Docker.

Conceptually:

```dockerfile
FROM <build-image> AS build

# compile/test/package

FROM <runtime-image>

# copy only runtime artifact
```

The final production image should not contain Maven merely because Maven was required during compilation.

---

# 9. Build Stage

The Java build stage requires:

```text
JDK 21
Maven
Source code
Dependencies
Build tooling
```

The runtime stage generally requires:

```text
Java runtime
Application artifact
Runtime configuration
```

This separation reduces image size and attack surface.

---

# 10. JDK vs Runtime Image

Production Spring Boot containers do not normally need:

```text
javac
Maven
Git
curl
build toolchains
```

unless there is a specific operational requirement.

Use the smallest supported runtime that satisfies application requirements.

---

# 11. Java 21

ADR-011 selected Java 21.

Therefore:

```text
Build Runtime → Java 21-compatible JDK
Application Runtime → Java 21-compatible runtime
```

Build/runtime compatibility must be enforced.

This prevents failures such as:

```text
UnsupportedClassVersionError
```

caused by compiling with a newer Java version than the runtime supports.

---

# 12. Base Image Strategy

Base images must be deliberately selected.

Candidates may include:

```text
Temurin
Microsoft Build of OpenJDK
Amazon Corretto
Distroless Java
Other approved OpenJDK distributions
```

The organization should standardize a small approved set.

---

# 13. Base Image Sprawl

Bad:

```text
Service A → Ubuntu + Java
Service B → Alpine + Java
Service C → Debian + Java
Service D → random Docker Hub image
```

This increases:

* CVE management
* Debugging complexity
* Patch workload
* Runtime differences
* Supply-chain risk

---

# 14. Alpine vs Debian

Alpine is not automatically superior merely because it is smaller.

Trade-offs include:

| Concern           | Alpine               | Debian/Ubuntu-family |
| ----------------- | -------------------- | -------------------- |
| Size              | Usually smaller      | Usually larger       |
| libc              | musl                 | glibc                |
| Compatibility     | Can be problematic   | Broad                |
| Debug familiarity | Lower for many teams | Higher               |
| Native libraries  | May require care     | Usually easier       |

Mediverse shall prioritize **compatibility and maintainability over image-size obsession**.

---

# 15. Distroless

Distroless images may reduce unnecessary runtime tooling and attack surface.

But they make interactive debugging harder.

Therefore:

```text
Distroless
    │
    └── Evaluate for production workloads
```

rather than forcing it universally.

---

# 16. Base Image Pinning

Production builds should avoid uncontrolled floating dependencies.

Weak:

```dockerfile
FROM eclipse-temurin:21
```

Stronger reproducibility may use controlled versions and/or digest pinning.

```text
Repository
+
Version
+
Digest
```

Digest pinning policy should balance reproducibility with security-patch automation.

---

# 17. `latest`

Production deployments shall not depend on:

```text
mediverse/content-service:latest
```

`latest` does not identify an immutable release.

---

# 18. Image Tagging

Images should support meaningful identifiers such as:

```text
1.4.2
1.4.2-rc.3
git-8f3c21a
```

Tags are human-readable references.

The image digest is the immutable identity.

---

# 19. Image Digest

Conceptually:

```text
content-service:1.4.2
        │
        ▼
sha256:...
```

Production deployment systems should be capable of identifying the exact digest deployed.

---

# 20. Immutable Images

Once:

```text
content-service:1.4.2
```

has been released, it shall not later be silently replaced with different image content.

That destroys traceability.

---

# 21. Build Once

Correct:

```text
Git Commit
    │
    ▼
Build Image
    │
    ▼
Registry
    │
    ├── DEV
    ├── UAT
    └── PROD
```

Incorrect:

```text
DEV  → build image

UAT  → build another image

PROD → build another image
```

Even with identical source code, these are not guaranteed to be identical artifacts.

---

# 22. Environment Configuration

Environment differences belong outside the image.

```text
Same Image
   │
   ├── DEV Configuration
   ├── UAT Configuration
   └── PROD Configuration
```

---

# 23. Configuration Sources

Runtime configuration may come from:

```text
Environment Variables
Kubernetes ConfigMaps
Kubernetes Secrets
External Secrets Management
Spring configuration
```

depending on sensitivity and architecture.

---

# 24. No Environment-Baked Images

Prohibited:

```text
content-service-dev:1.0
content-service-uat:1.0
content-service-prod:1.0
```

where differences exist merely because environment configuration was embedded during build.

---

# 25. Secrets

Secrets must never be baked into images.

Prohibited:

```dockerfile
ENV DB_PASSWORD=my-password
ENV OPENAI_API_KEY=...
ENV KEYCLOAK_SECRET=...
```

---

# 26. Secrets in Layers

Deleting a secret in a later Docker layer does not necessarily remove it from image history.

Bad:

```dockerfile
COPY secrets.txt .
RUN use-secret
RUN rm secrets.txt
```

The secret may remain recoverable from previous layers.

---

# 27. Build Secrets

If private dependencies require credentials during builds, use secure build-secret mechanisms rather than:

```text
ARG PASSWORD
COPY settings-with-password.xml
```

where secrets can leak into build history or logs.

---

# 28. `.dockerignore`

Every build context should exclude unnecessary files.

Typical exclusions include:

```text
.git
.idea
.vscode
node_modules
target where appropriate
local secrets
logs
test output
temporary files
```

A small build context improves performance and reduces accidental secret inclusion.

---

# 29. Docker Build Context

Do not use the entire monorepository as the build context when a service only requires a small subset unless repository architecture requires it.

Large contexts slow builds and increase accidental exposure.

---

# 30. Maven Dependency Caching

Dockerfiles should be structured to avoid redownloading the entire Maven dependency graph after every source-code modification.

Conceptually:

```text
pom.xml
   │
   ▼
Resolve dependencies
   │
   ▼
Copy source
   │
   ▼
Compile
```

This allows dependency layers to remain cached when only source code changes.

---

# 31. BuildKit Cache

CI should use BuildKit-compatible caching where practical.

```text
Maven dependencies
Docker layers
Frontend dependencies
```

can significantly reduce build time.

---

# 32. Cache Correctness

Caching must not sacrifice correctness.

A 30-second build producing stale artifacts is worse than a 5-minute correct build.

---

# 33. Spring Boot Layering

Spring Boot application layers can separate:

```text
Dependencies
Spring Boot loader
Snapshot dependencies
Application code
```

allowing frequently changing application code to occupy different image layers from stable dependencies.

---

# 34. Layer Efficiency

Without useful layering:

```text
1 source change
     │
     ▼
Entire 300 MB layer changes
```

With sensible layering:

```text
Dependencies → cached
Application  → changed
```

This improves registry and deployment efficiency.

---

# 35. Image Size

Image size matters, but it is not the only goal.

Optimize for:

```text
Security
Compatibility
Startup
Network transfer
Operational support
Build speed
```

not merely the smallest number shown by `docker images`.

---

# 36. Non-Root Containers

Application containers should run as non-root by default.

Bad:

```text
UID 0
```

Preferred:

```text
Dedicated application UID
```

unless a documented technical requirement requires elevated privileges.

---

# 37. Root Risk

A container is not a complete security boundary.

Running as root unnecessarily increases impact if the application is compromised.

---

# 38. Privileged Containers

Mediverse application containers shall not run with:

```text
privileged: true
```

without exceptional infrastructure justification.

Ordinary Spring Boot services do not need privileged containers.

---

# 39. Linux Capabilities

Unnecessary Linux capabilities should be removed where Kubernetes/container security policy permits.

Least privilege applies below the application layer too.

---

# 40. Read-Only Root Filesystem

Production application containers should support:

```text
readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

where feasible.

Applications requiring temporary writes should use explicitly designated writable locations.

---

# 41. Temporary Files

If a service needs temporary storage:

```text
/tmp
```

or equivalent should be explicitly managed.

Kubernetes `emptyDir` may be appropriate for ephemeral scratch space.

---

# 42. Persistent Data

Application containers shall not store durable business state inside their writable container filesystem.

Bad:

```text
/content-service/data/database.db
```

The container filesystem is ephemeral.

---

# 43. Persistent Storage Boundary

Durable state belongs to:

```text
PostgreSQL
Redis where appropriate
Kafka
Object Storage
Persistent Volumes where justified
```

not arbitrary container layers.

---

# 44. Stateless Application Containers

Spring Boot services should remain stateless wherever practical.

```text
Request
   │
   ▼
Any healthy replica
```

This supports horizontal scaling.

---

# 45. Session State

Do not store user sessions in one gateway/application container's memory if requests must survive pod replacement or load balancing.

ADR-028 already assigns identity sessions primarily to Keycloak.

---

# 46. Logging

Application containers shall log primarily to:

```text
stdout
stderr
```

rather than maintaining permanent log files inside the container.

---

# 47. Log Collection

```text
Application
    │
    ▼
stdout/stderr
    │
    ▼
Container Runtime
    │
    ▼
Kubernetes Logging Pipeline
    │
    ▼
Central Log Platform
```

This keeps application images independent of logging vendors.

---

# 48. No Permanent `/logs`

Avoid:

```text
/app/logs/application.log
```

as the only logging destination.

Container deletion would remove the logs unless external persistence existed.

---

# 49. Structured Logging

Services should prefer structured logs suitable for centralized ingestion.

Example conceptual fields:

```text
timestamp
level
service
traceId
correlationId
message
```

Sensitive data rules from ADR-028/029 still apply.

---

# 50. Health Checks

Container health behavior should align with Spring Boot Actuator/Kubernetes probes.

```text
Liveness
Readiness
Startup
```

solve different problems.

---

# 51. Docker `HEALTHCHECK`

Docker health checks can help in standalone Docker environments.

Kubernetes deployments should rely primarily on Kubernetes probe configuration appropriate to the workload.

Do not create conflicting health systems.

---

# 52. Startup Probe

Slow-starting workloads may require a startup probe.

This prevents Kubernetes from repeatedly killing a healthy application simply because initialization takes time.

---

# 53. Readiness Probe

Readiness determines whether a container should receive traffic.

```text
Ready
  │
  ▼
Service traffic

Not Ready
  │
  X
Traffic
```

---

# 54. Liveness Probe

Liveness answers whether the process is irrecoverably unhealthy and should be restarted.

Do not make liveness depend on every external service.

---

# 55. PostgreSQL Failure Example

Bad:

```text
PostgreSQL temporarily unavailable
        │
        ▼
Liveness fails
        │
        ▼
Every service pod restarts
```

This can create a restart storm during a database outage.

---

# 56. Graceful Shutdown

Spring Boot containers must support graceful termination.

```text
SIGTERM
   │
   ▼
Stop accepting new work
   │
   ▼
Complete bounded active work
   │
   ▼
Shutdown
```

---

# 57. SIGKILL

Applications must not rely on receiving unlimited shutdown time.

Kubernetes eventually terminates processes that exceed the grace period.

---

# 58. PID 1

Container entrypoints must correctly handle Unix signals.

Avoid unnecessary shell wrappers that interfere with signal propagation.

---

# 59. JVM Container Awareness

Java 21 understands container resource constraints.

However, correct Kubernetes memory limits and JVM behavior still require engineering.

---

# 60. JVM Memory

A container with:

```text
memory limit = 1 GiB
```

cannot safely assign the entire 1 GiB to Java heap.

Memory is also required for:

```text
Metaspace
Thread stacks
Direct buffers
Native libraries
JIT
GC structures
```

---

# 61. `-Xmx` Mistake

Bad:

```text
Container memory = 1Gi
-Xmx1g
```

This leaves effectively no headroom for non-heap/native memory and can trigger container OOM termination.

---

# 62. Percentage-Based JVM Memory

Modern JVM container options such as percentage-based heap sizing may be preferable to hard-coded memory values for some workloads.

Exact settings must be validated under realistic load.

---

# 63. OOMKilled

Kubernetes:

```text
OOMKilled
```

is not necessarily a Java `OutOfMemoryError`.

The Linux container memory limit may terminate the process before Java reports a heap failure.

Operations must distinguish the two.

---

# 64. CPU Limits

CPU limits affect JVM scheduling and latency.

Aggressively constraining CPU can create:

```text
Throttling
Long GC pauses
Slow request handling
Timeouts
```

even when average CPU appears acceptable.

---

# 65. Resource Requests and Limits

Every production workload should have intentional:

```text
requests:
  cpu
  memory

limits:
  memory
  cpu where policy requires
```

based on measured behavior rather than arbitrary copied values.

---

# 66. React/Vite Build

ADR-024 selected Vite.

Frontend build:

```text
React + TypeScript
      │
      ▼
Vite Build
      │
      ▼
Static Assets
```

These assets do not require Node.js at runtime if deployed as a normal SPA.

---

# 67. Frontend Multi-Stage Build

Conceptually:

```text
Node Build Stage
      │
      ▼
npm install/build
      │
      ▼
dist/
      │
      ▼
Static Runtime
```

Node development dependencies should not automatically exist in the production runtime.

---

# 68. Frontend Runtime

Possible frontend deployment:

```text
Browser
   │
   ▼
CDN
```

or:

```text
Browser
   │
   ▼
NGINX Container
   │
   ▼
Static Vite Assets
```

The preferred architecture should increasingly favor CDN delivery for scalable static assets.

---

# 69. Frontend Environment Variables

Vite environment values embedded during build become part of the frontend bundle.

They are not secrets.

Never put:

```text
DB_PASSWORD
CLIENT_SECRET
PRIVATE_API_KEY
```

into frontend Vite variables.

---

# 70. Frontend Runtime Configuration

If the exact same frontend image must move between environments, runtime-injected public configuration may be required.

This should be designed explicitly rather than rebuilding the frontend for every environment.

---

# 71. Source Maps

Production source-map publication requires deliberate security/debugging policy.

Source maps can significantly improve error diagnosis but may expose implementation details.

---

# 72. AI/Python Containers

AI workloads may use separate Python containers.

```text
AI Service
   │
   ├── Python runtime
   ├── Dependencies
   └── Application
```

They should follow the same principles:

* Minimal images
* Non-root
* Pinned dependencies
* Immutable artifacts
* Scanning
* Reproducibility

---

# 73. Python Dependency Pinning

AI images must not rely casually on:

```text
pip install latest-everything
```

Production dependencies require deterministic version management.

---

# 74. ML Model Packaging

Large ML models should not automatically be embedded inside application images.

Consider:

```text
Object Storage
Model Registry
Persistent model cache
Dedicated inference infrastructure
```

depending on model size and deployment requirements.

---

# 75. Image Explosion

Embedding a multi-gigabyte model into every image revision causes:

```text
Slow builds
Huge registry storage
Slow deployment
Slow node pulls
```

Model lifecycle and application lifecycle may differ.

---

# 76. Native Dependencies

Python/AI workloads may require:

```text
CUDA
BLAS
native libraries
```

Base images must match actual runtime infrastructure.

Do not use GPU images for CPU-only workloads.

---

# 77. Multi-Architecture Images

Mediverse should retain the ability to publish images for architectures such as:

```text
linux/amd64
linux/arm64
```

where deployment infrastructure requires them.

---

# 78. Architecture Consistency

Do not accidentally build a developer's ARM laptop image and expect an AMD64 production cluster to run it.

CI should explicitly control target platforms.

---

# 79. Image Registry

All production images shall reside in an approved container registry.

Conceptually:

```text
CI
 │
 ▼
Container Registry
 │
 ├── gateway
 ├── content-service
 ├── assessment-service
 ├── ai-service
 └── frontend
```

---

# 80. Nexus Relationship

If Mediverse adopts Nexus as an artifact repository, its container registry capabilities may be evaluated.

Registry selection must consider:

```text
Availability
Security
RBAC
Scanning integration
Replication
Retention
Performance
Backup
```

---

# 81. Public Registry Dependency

Production deployment should not depend directly on arbitrary public Docker Hub availability for Mediverse-owned application images.

Approved base images may be mirrored where supply-chain policy requires it.

---

# 82. Registry Authentication

Push and pull access must use controlled identities.

```text
Developer
CI
Kubernetes
```

should not all share one permanent registry administrator password.

---

# 83. Registry RBAC

Permissions should separate:

```text
Push
Pull
Delete
Admin
```

according to responsibility.

---

# 84. Image Retention

Registries require retention policies.

Keeping every CI image forever eventually creates unnecessary cost and operational clutter.

But production-referenced artifacts must not be deleted prematurely.

---

# 85. Artifact Traceability

For any production pod, operations should be able to answer:

```text
Which Git commit?

Which CI build?

Which image digest?

Which dependencies?

Which SBOM?

Which security scan?

Who approved promotion?
```

---

# 86. Image Labels

OCI image metadata may include:

```text
source repository
revision
version
build timestamp
vendor
```

where useful.

Do not place secrets in image labels.

---

# 87. SBOM

Every production image should support generation of a **Software Bill of Materials**.

```text
Image
  │
  ▼
SBOM
  │
  ├── OS packages
  ├── Java dependencies
  └── Other components
```

This becomes critical when a new vulnerability is announced.

---

# 88. Why SBOM Matters

Suppose a critical library vulnerability appears.

Without SBOM:

```text
"Which 70 services contain it?"
        │
        ▼
Manual investigation
```

With searchable SBOM data, affected artifacts can be identified much faster.

---

# 89. SBOM Formats

Industry-standard formats such as:

```text
CycloneDX
SPDX
```

should be preferred.

The exact tooling belongs to DevSecOps implementation.

---

# 90. Vulnerability Scanning

Container images must be scanned before production promotion.

Potential tooling includes:

```text
Trivy
Grype
Registry-native scanners
```

Tool selection may evolve without changing the architectural requirement.

---

# 91. Scan Scope

Scanning should cover:

```text
Operating-system packages
Java dependencies
Node dependencies
Python dependencies
Known vulnerabilities
```

where supported.

---

# 92. Scan Policy

A vulnerability scanner producing 500 findings is useless unless policy defines what happens next.

Policy must define:

```text
Severity threshold
Exploitability consideration
Exceptions
Expiration of exceptions
Remediation SLA
Production blocking criteria
```

---

# 93. CVE False Positives

Not every scanner finding means the application is exploitable.

Security review should distinguish:

```text
Package present
        ≠
Vulnerability reachable/exploitable
```

But "probably false positive" is not a valid reason to ignore findings indefinitely.

---

# 94. Image Signing

Production supply-chain architecture should support cryptographic image signing.

Conceptually:

```text
CI
 │
 ▼
Image
 │
 ▼
Sign
 │
 ▼
Registry
```

---

# 95. Sigstore/Cosign Direction

Sigstore/Cosign-style signing and verification should be evaluated for Mediverse.

The objective is not tool adoption for its own sake.

The objective is:

> Kubernetes should eventually be able to verify that deployed images came from an approved build process.

---

# 96. Build Provenance

Production artifacts should support provenance attestation describing:

```text
Source
Build system
Commit
Build parameters
Artifact
```

This strengthens software supply-chain integrity.

---

# 97. Admission Control

A future Kubernetes security architecture may enforce:

```text
Unsigned image
      │
      X
Deployment

Approved signed image
      │
      ▼
Deployment
```

through admission policies.

This belongs to a later Kubernetes/security ADR.

---

# 98. Dependency Supply Chain

Container security is not only about the base image.

A compromised:

```text
Maven dependency
npm package
Python package
GitHub action
CI plugin
```

can compromise the resulting image.

---

# 99. Dependency Locking

Frontend and Python builds should use appropriate lockfiles.

Maven dependency versions should be centrally and explicitly governed.

Dynamic production dependencies should be minimized.

---

# 100. Maven Snapshot Dependencies

Production releases should not depend casually on:

```text
1.0-SNAPSHOT
```

from mutable remote repositories.

Released artifacts should be reproducible.

---

# 101. Build Network Access

CI builds should access only approved dependency repositories where practical.

Unrestricted package retrieval increases supply-chain exposure.

---

# 102. Private Maven Repository

If Mediverse uses Nexus:

```text
CI
 │
 ▼
Nexus
 │
 ├── Maven Central proxy
 ├── Internal libraries
 └── Controlled dependencies
```

This can improve governance and caching.

---

# 103. Image Promotion

Artifact lifecycle:

```text
BUILD
  │
  ▼
SCAN
  │
  ▼
SIGN
  │
  ▼
DEV
  │
  ▼
UAT
  │
  ▼
PROD
```

Promotion changes deployment references/configuration—not application binaries.

---

# 104. Production Promotion

A production deployment should reference the already-tested artifact.

```text
UAT tested digest:
sha256:ABC...
       │
       ▼
PROD:
sha256:ABC...
```

not:

```text
Rebuild source
       │
       ▼
sha256:XYZ...
```

---

# 105. Rollback

Immutable images simplify rollback.

```text
Current
sha256:BBB

Previous
sha256:AAA
```

Rollback means redeploying the previous approved artifact.

---

# 106. Rollback Limitation

Application rollback does not automatically mean database rollback.

If release `BBB` performs incompatible schema migration, redeploying image `AAA` may fail.

Database migration compatibility requires a separate ADR.

---

# 107. Semantic Versioning

Human-facing release tags should use a consistent version strategy.

Example:

```text
2.3.1
```

can represent:

```text
MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
```

where semantic versioning fits the service's release model.

---

# 108. Git SHA

Git SHA tags improve traceability.

Example:

```text
content-service:git-a17f93c
```

This allows direct mapping from image to source revision.

---

# 109. Multiple Tags

The same immutable digest may have multiple references:

```text
content-service:2.4.1
content-service:git-a17f93c
```

Both may point to:

```text
sha256:ABC...
```

That is acceptable.

---

# 110. Release Candidate

Pre-production releases may use:

```text
2.4.1-rc.1
```

or equivalent controlled naming.

The naming convention should be consistent across services.

---

# 111. `latest` Policy

`latest` may be tolerated for local developer convenience.

It shall not be used as the authoritative production deployment reference.

---

# 112. Docker Compose

Docker Compose shall remain useful for local development and integration environments.

Example:

```text
Docker Compose
   │
   ├── PostgreSQL
   ├── Redis
   ├── Kafka
   ├── Keycloak
   └── Selected services
```

---

# 113. Compose Is Not Production Kubernetes

Do not attempt to make local Compose topology identical to production Kubernetes.

The goal is developer productivity and useful behavioral similarity—not fake production infrastructure.

---

# 114. Local Dependencies

Developers should be able to start required infrastructure predictably.

```text
docker compose up
```

should provide repeatable dependencies where feasible.

---

# 115. Testcontainers

Integration tests should evaluate Testcontainers for infrastructure dependencies.

Example:

```text
JUnit
  │
  ├── PostgreSQL Container
  ├── Redis Container
  └── Kafka Container
```

This often provides stronger integration tests than mocked infrastructure.

---

# 116. Testcontainers Advantage

Tests can run against real technology versions rather than:

```text
Mock PostgreSQL
Mock Kafka
Mock Redis
```

which may behave differently from production.

---

# 117. CI Container Builds

CI should perform:

```text
Checkout
   │
   ▼
Compile
   │
   ▼
Unit Tests
   │
   ▼
Integration Tests
   │
   ▼
Image Build
   │
   ▼
Scan
   │
   ▼
SBOM
   │
   ▼
Sign
   │
   ▼
Push
```

The exact ordering may vary depending on pipeline architecture.

---

# 118. CI Build Isolation

Build workers should be ephemeral or sufficiently isolated.

Persistent shared build environments increase contamination and credential-leak risk.

---

# 119. Docker Socket Risk

Mounting:

```text
/var/run/docker.sock
```

into arbitrary CI containers effectively grants powerful host-level access.

CI architecture must treat Docker daemon access as privileged.

---

# 120. Docker-in-Docker

Docker-in-Docker can work but introduces security, caching and operational trade-offs.

CI container build architecture should be selected explicitly rather than copied from tutorials.

---

# 121. Build Alternatives

OCI images can also be built using:

```text
BuildKit
Kaniko-style builders
Buildah
Cloud-native builders
```

depending on CI infrastructure.

Docker CLI compatibility is not an architectural requirement.

---

# 122. Reproducibility

A strong build should minimize uncontrolled inputs:

```text
Source
Dependency versions
Base image
Build tools
Configuration
```

The fewer floating dependencies, the more reproducible the artifact.

---

# 123. Build Timestamp

Perfect byte-for-byte reproducibility can be complicated by timestamps and metadata.

Mediverse should prioritize meaningful artifact reproducibility and provenance, not chase theoretical reproducibility without business value.

---

# 124. Base Image Updates

Digest pinning creates a responsibility:

```text
Pinned image
    │
    ▼
Does not automatically receive security patches
```

Therefore automated update monitoring is required.

---

# 125. Security Rebuild

If the Java runtime base image receives a critical CVE fix:

```text
Application code unchanged
       │
       ▼
Rebuild image
       │
       ▼
New artifact
```

A new release may be required even without application-code changes.

---

# 126. Patch Cadence

Images should be rebuilt periodically to absorb:

```text
OS fixes
JVM fixes
Security patches
Dependency fixes
```

Immutable does not mean never updated.

It means released artifacts are not mutated.

---

# 127. Emergency Rebuild

Critical supply-chain vulnerabilities require an accelerated rebuild path.

The CI/CD architecture must not require weeks of manual work to patch a base image.

---

# 128. End-of-Life Images

Unsupported Java/OS base images shall be removed from the approved catalog.

Running an image indefinitely because "it still works" is not a security strategy.

---

# 129. Image Scanning After Build

Security does not stop when the image enters the registry.

A previously clean image can become vulnerable when new CVEs are discovered.

Registries/security systems should support periodic reassessment.

---

# 130. Runtime Security

Image scanning cannot detect every runtime attack.

Runtime controls remain necessary:

```text
Kubernetes securityContext
NetworkPolicy
RBAC
Secrets
Admission policies
Monitoring
Runtime detection
```

---

# 131. Kubernetes Security Context

Production application workloads should generally aim for:

```text
runAsNonRoot
allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
readOnlyRootFilesystem where feasible
drop unnecessary capabilities
```

Exact manifests belong to Kubernetes/DIG documentation.

---

# 132. Container User

Application images should define or support a stable non-root UID/GID strategy compatible with Kubernetes.

Avoid relying solely on username semantics that may differ between images.

---

# 133. Port Binding

Non-root containers should use unprivileged ports internally where practical.

Example:

```text
8080
```

rather than requiring root simply to bind port 80.

Ingress/service mapping can expose standard external ports.

---

# 134. Container Filesystem Ownership

Applications should not require:

```text
chmod -R 777 /
```

to start.

Filesystem permissions must be designed correctly.

---

# 135. Runtime Package Installation

Production containers should not execute:

```text
apt install ...
npm install ...
pip install ...
```

during startup.

All required software belongs in the immutable build artifact.

---

# 136. Shell Access

Production applications should not require interactive shell access to function.

Debugging should rely primarily on:

```text
Logs
Metrics
Traces
Ephemeral debug tooling
```

This enables more minimal production images.

---

# 137. Container Naming

Image repositories should use consistent naming.

Example:

```text
mediverse/gateway
mediverse/content-service
mediverse/assessment-service
mediverse/learning-service
mediverse/ai-service
```

---

# 138. Ownership Metadata

Each image/repository should map to an owning engineering team or service owner.

Security findings without ownership become unresolved findings.

---

# 139. Container Contract

Every Mediverse application image should define:

```text
Entrypoint
Port(s)
Required configuration
Optional configuration
Health endpoint
Resource expectations
Shutdown behavior
Writable directories
External dependencies
```

This becomes part of the deployment contract.

---

# 140. Container Anti-Patterns

The following are prohibited or strongly discouraged:

❌ `latest` in production

❌ Secrets inside Dockerfiles

❌ Secrets copied into image layers

❌ Root containers without justification

❌ Privileged application containers

❌ Permanent business data in container filesystem

❌ Maven/JDK in runtime image without need

❌ Environment-specific application binaries

❌ Rebuilding separately for PROD

❌ Runtime package installation

❌ Random unapproved base images

❌ Unlimited image sizes

❌ Blind Alpine adoption because it is small

❌ Ignoring base-image CVEs

❌ Hardcoding `-Xmx` equal to container memory limit

❌ Logging only to container-local files

❌ One container containing application + DB + Redis

❌ Mutable release tags

❌ Public-registry credentials in source code

❌ CI secrets exposed through build arguments

❌ Shipping development tools unnecessarily

❌ Treating containerization as a complete security boundary

---

# 141. Security Architecture

```text
                     SOURCE
                       │
                       ▼
                 Dependency Scan
                       │
                       ▼
                    BUILD
                       │
                       ▼
                  OCI IMAGE
                       │
             ┌─────────┼─────────┐
             ▼         ▼         ▼
           SBOM       Scan    Provenance
             │         │         │
             └─────────┼─────────┘
                       ▼
                     SIGN
                       │
                       ▼
                   REGISTRY
                       │
                       ▼
               Admission Policy
                       │
                       ▼
                   KUBERNETES
                       │
                       ▼
               Runtime Security
```

This is the target DevSecOps direction.

---

# 142. Artifact Promotion Architecture

```text
Git Commit
    │
    ▼
CI Pipeline
    │
    ├── Build
    ├── Test
    ├── Scan
    ├── SBOM
    ├── Sign
    └── Push
    │
    ▼
Registry
    │
    │ image digest = sha256:ABC
    │
    ├──────────────► DEV
    │                 │
    │                 ▼
    │              Validate
    │
    ├──────────────► UAT
    │                 │
    │                 ▼
    │              Approve
    │
    └──────────────► PROD

         SAME DIGEST
         sha256:ABC
```

---

# 143. Risks and Mitigations

| Risk                      | Mitigation                      |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Vulnerable base image     | Scanning + automated rebuilds   |
| Supply-chain compromise   | SBOM + signing + provenance     |
| Secret leakage            | Build/runtime secret management |
| Root compromise           | Non-root runtime                |
| Mutable artifacts         | Immutable tags/digests          |
| Environment drift         | Same-image promotion            |
| Huge images               | Multi-stage builds + layering   |
| JVM OOM                   | Container-aware memory tuning   |
| Registry outage           | HA/DR strategy                  |
| Wrong architecture        | CI-controlled target platform   |
| Stale CVEs                | Continuous rescanning           |
| Slow CI                   | BuildKit/dependency caching     |
| Untraceable production    | Git SHA + digest + provenance   |
| Persistent data loss      | External persistence            |
| Build credential exposure | Build secrets                   |
| Container escape impact   | Least privilege + K8s security  |

---

# 144. Consequences

### Positive

* Reproducible deployments
* Environment consistency
* Kubernetes compatibility
* Horizontal scalability
* Faster rollback
* Better CI/CD
* Strong artifact traceability
* Improved supply-chain security
* Standardized runtime
* Easier vulnerability management
* Reduced configuration drift

### Negative

* Registry becomes critical infrastructure
* Container security requires ongoing maintenance
* Image vulnerabilities require rebuilds
* Multi-architecture builds add complexity
* Distroless/minimal images can complicate debugging
* CI requires secure container-building infrastructure
* Developers must understand container resource behavior

---

# 145. Decision Outcome

| Attribute                   | Decision                              |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| **ADR**                     | ADR-030                               |
| **Packaging Standard**      | OCI Container Images                  |
| **Primary Build Workflow**  | Docker-compatible                     |
| **Java**                    | Java 21                               |
| **Build Strategy**          | Multi-stage                           |
| **Runtime Images**          | Minimal approved runtime              |
| **Execution User**          | Non-root                              |
| **Artifact Mutability**     | Immutable                             |
| **Production `latest`**     | Prohibited                            |
| **Versioning**              | SemVer + Git SHA + digest             |
| **Environment Strategy**    | Same image, external configuration    |
| **Secrets in Image**        | Prohibited                            |
| **SBOM**                    | Required direction                    |
| **Vulnerability Scan**      | Required                              |
| **Signing/Provenance**      | Production target                     |
| **Registry**                | Approved private registry             |
| **Persistent App Data**     | External only                         |
| **Logging**                 | stdout/stderr                         |
| **Runtime Package Install** | Prohibited                            |
| **Local Development**       | Docker Compose                        |
| **Integration Testing**     | Testcontainers preferred where useful |
| **Deployment Target**       | Kubernetes                            |
| **Status**                  | Accepted                              |
| **Priority**                | Critical                              |
| **Risk Level**              | High                                  |

---

# 146. Final Container Architecture

```text
                         MEDIVERSE SOURCE
                               │
                               ▼
                         ┌───────────┐
                         │ CI SYSTEM │
                         └─────┬─────┘
                               │
             ┌─────────────────┼─────────────────┐
             ▼                 ▼                 ▼
          Maven              Node              Python
             │                 │                 │
             ▼                 ▼                 ▼
        Spring Boot          React             AI
             │                 │                 │
             └─────────────────┼─────────────────┘
                               ▼
                         OCI IMAGE BUILD
                               │
                    ┌──────────┼──────────┐
                    ▼          ▼          ▼
                   SBOM       Scan    Provenance
                    │          │          │
                    └──────────┼──────────┘
                               ▼
                             SIGN
                               │
                               ▼
                    ┌──────────────────┐
                    │ PRIVATE REGISTRY │
                    └────────┬─────────┘
                             │
              ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐

              │              │              │
              └──────────────┼──────────────┘
                             │

                             │
                             ▼

```

---

# 147. Runtime Architecture

```text
                  Kubernetes Pod
                       │
             ┌─────────▼─────────┐
             │ Application Image │
             │                   │
             │ Non-root          │
             │ Immutable         │
             │ Minimal runtime   │
             │ Java 21           │
             └─────────┬─────────┘
                       │
          ┌────────────┼────────────┐
          ▼            ▼            ▼
      ConfigMap      Secret      Observability
          │            │            │
          ▼            ▼            ▼
      Runtime       Runtime     stdout/metrics
      Config        Secret        /traces
                       │
                       ▼
              External Dependencies
                       │
       ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
       ▼               ▼               ▼
   PostgreSQL        Redis          Kafka/Object
                                     Storage
```

The container itself remains disposable.

---

# 148. Core Container Rules

```text
             MEDIVERSE CONTAINER CONTRACT

 Build once                              ✅
 Promote same artifact                   ✅
 Immutable images                        ✅
 External configuration                  ✅
 Non-root                                ✅
 Minimal runtime                         ✅
 SBOM                                    ✅
 Vulnerability scanning                  ✅
 Artifact traceability                   ✅
 Graceful shutdown                       ✅
 stdout/stderr logging                   ✅

 Secrets in image                        ❌
 Production :latest                      ❌
 Root by default                         ❌
 Runtime package installation            ❌
 Persistent business data in container   ❌
 Separate PROD rebuild                   ❌
 Mutable released image                  ❌
```

---
