```text
Maximum payload size
Dependency budget
Throughput target
Error-rate target
```

"Fast" is not a measurable requirement.

---

# 143. API Ownership

Every production API requires an accountable owner.

```text
API
 │
 ├── Owning team
 ├── Repository
 ├── Documentation
 ├── On-call path
 ├── Contract
 └── Lifecycle status
```

Orphaned APIs become security and operational liabilities.

---

# 144. API Catalog

At sufficient scale, Mediverse should maintain an API catalog containing:

```text
API name
Owner
Domain
Classification
Protocol
Version
Consumers
Authentication
Documentation
Lifecycle state
```

This supports discoverability and governance.

---

# 145. API Lifecycle

```text
Design
  │
  ▼
Review
  │
  ▼
Implement
  │
  ▼
Test
  │
  ▼
Publish
  │
  ▼
Observe
  │
  ▼
Evolve
  │
  ▼
Deprecate
  │
  ▼
Retire
```

APIs require lifecycle management beyond implementation.

---

# 146. API Governance

Governance should enforce minimum standards without creating an architecture committee bottleneck for every endpoint.

Automate:

```text
Schema linting
Compatibility checks
Security checks
Contract tests
Documentation validation
Ownership metadata
```

Use human review for high-impact design decisions.

---

# 147. API Anti-Patterns

Mediverse rejects:

```text
❌ POST for every operation
❌ 200 for every outcome
❌ Database entities exposed directly
❌ Business logic in API Gateway
❌ Gateway authentication treated as complete authorization
❌ UUIDs treated as authorization
❌ Unbounded collection endpoints
❌ Unlimited page sizes
❌ Arbitrary SQL-like filtering
❌ Uncontrolled bulk operations
❌ Retryable side effects without idempotency strategy
❌ Infinite/stacked retries
❌ Synchronous calls without timeouts
❌ Internal APIs treated as disposable contracts
❌ OpenAPI documentation drifting from implementation
❌ Breaking API changes without consumer analysis
❌ New major version for trivial additive changes
❌ APIs deprecated forever but never removed
❌ GraphQL introduced merely to replace REST
❌ GraphQL resolver N+1 ignored
❌ Unlimited GraphQL query depth/complexity
❌ GraphQL gateway becoming domain owner
❌ gRPC introduced everywhere because it benchmarks faster
❌ Protobuf field numbers reused
❌ gRPC calls without deadlines
❌ WebSockets used when SSE is sufficient
❌ WebSocket channel name treated as authorization
❌ Infinite reconnect loops
❌ Unlimited real-time buffering
❌ Core transactions blocked on external webhooks
❌ Unsigned webhooks
❌ Webhook duplicates assumed impossible
❌ BFF becoming a giant business-logic service
❌ Entire internal objects returned to clients
❌ Shared caching of sensitive personalized responses
❌ No API owner
❌ No consumer inventory
```

---

# 148. Final Mediverse Enterprise API Reference Architecture

```text
                             CONSUMERS
             ┌──────────────────┼───────────────────┐
             ▼                  ▼                   ▼
            WEB               MOBILE             PARTNER
             │                  │                   │
             └──────────────────┼───────────────────┘
                                ▼
                        CDN / EDGE SECURITY
                                │
                                ▼
                           API GATEWAY
                                │
          ┌─────────────────────┼──────────────────────┐
          ▼                     ▼                      ▼
        REST                 GraphQL             REAL-TIME
          │                     │                 ┌────┴────┐
          │                     │                 ▼         ▼
          │                     │             WebSocket    SSE
          │                     │
          └─────────────────────┼──────────────────────┐
                                ▼                      │
                         BFF / COMPOSITION             │
                                │                      │
                                ▼                      │
                         DOMAIN SERVICES ◄─────────────┘
                                │
              ┌─────────────────┼─────────────────┐
              ▼                 ▼                 ▼
             REST              gRPC             EVENTS
              │                 │                 │
              │                 │                 ▼
              │                 │             Kafka/Broker
              │                 │                 │
              │                 │        ┌────────┴────────┐
              │                 │        ▼                 ▼
              │                 │     Workers          Webhooks
              │                 │
              └─────────────────┼────────────────────────────┐
                                ▼                            │
                         DOMAIN / DATA                       │
                                                             │
                                                             ▼
                                                     EXTERNAL SYSTEMS


                         CROSS-CUTTING CONTROL

        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ Authentication / Authorization                     │
        │ Rate Limits / Quotas                               │
        │ Validation                                         │
        │ Idempotency                                        │
        │ Timeouts / Deadlines                               │
        │ Retries / Circuit Breakers                         │
        │ Trace Context                                      │
        │ Logging / Metrics                                  │
        │ OpenAPI / Protobuf / GraphQL Contracts             │
        │ Compatibility                                      │
        │ Security                                           │
        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘


                         GOVERNANCE PLANE

        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ API Catalog                                        │
        │ Ownership                                          │
        │ Contract Registry                                  │
        │ Schema Linting                                     │
        │ Breaking-Change Detection                          │
        │ Consumer Inventory                                 │
        │ Documentation                                      │
        │ Deprecation / Sunset                               │
        │ SLOs                                               │
        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

# 149. Core API Invariants

Regardless of future frameworks or gateway products:

```text
1. Every API is a contract.

2. Internal APIs are still contracts.

3. REST remains the default conventional API style.

4. Protocol choice follows workload requirements.

5. HTTP semantics are respected.

6. Persistence models do not become external contracts.

7. Inputs are validated at trust boundaries.

8. Domain invariants remain domain responsibilities.

9. Object-level authorization is mandatory.

10. Collections are bounded and paginated.

11. Retryable side effects have idempotency strategy.

12. Every synchronous dependency has a timeout/deadline.

13. Retries are bounded and coordinated.

14. API Gateway does not own domain business logic.

15. GraphQL is introduced only where consumer composition warrants it.

16. GraphQL query cost is controlled.

17. GraphQL authorization remains resource-aware.

18. gRPC contracts evolve compatibly.

19. gRPC calls have deadlines.

20. Real-time connections have authentication,
    authorization and lifecycle controls.

21. Backpressure is explicit.

22. Webhooks are signed, retryable and duplicate-safe.

23. Synchronous chains are kept shallow.

24. Events are preferred when immediate responses are unnecessary.

25. BFFs shape consumer experiences but do not own core domains.

26. API evolution prefers additive compatibility.

27. Breaking changes are automatically detected.

28. Deprecation includes migration and sunset.

29. Important consumers are inventoried.

30. API performance is measured through explicit SLOs.

31. Sensitive responses are not carelessly cached.

32. Every production API has an accountable owner.

33. Contracts, documentation and implementation remain synchronized.

34. API security is continuously tested.

35. API governance is automated wherever practical.
```

---

# 150. Decision Outcome

| Area                                  | Decision                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Primary application API               | **REST/HTTPS**                                         |
| REST design                           | Resource-oriented                                      |
| HTTP semantics                        | Mandatory                                              |
| API entities                          | Explicit DTOs                                          |
| Problem responses                     | Standardized Problem Details                           |
| Validation                            | Boundary + domain                                      |
| Pagination                            | Mandatory for growing collections                      |
| Offset pagination                     | Standard/simple workloads                              |
| Cursor pagination                     | Large/high-change datasets                             |
| Idempotency                           | Required where retries can duplicate effects           |
| OpenAPI                               | Required for REST                                      |
| API Gateway                           | Edge/API-management concerns                           |
| Business logic in gateway             | Rejected                                               |
| GraphQL                               | Selective composition layer                            |
| GraphQL as universal REST replacement | Rejected                                               |
| GraphQL complexity controls           | Required                                               |
| GraphQL federation                    | Only when organizational scale justifies               |
| gRPC                                  | Selective internal communication                       |
| Protobuf compatibility                | Mandatory                                              |
| gRPC deadlines                        | Mandatory                                              |
| WebSockets                            | Bidirectional real-time workloads                      |
| SSE                                   | Preferred for simpler server→client streams            |
| WebSocket auth                        | Connection + resource authorization                    |
| Backpressure                          | Explicit                                               |
| Webhooks                              | Async + signed + retryable                             |
| Webhook delivery                      | At-least-once assumption                               |
| Sync communication                    | Immediate-result workflows                             |
| Async communication                   | Decoupled/background workflows                         |
| BFF                                   | Client-specific composition                            |
| API evolution                         | Additive first                                         |
| Major versions                        | Breaking changes only                                  |
| Contract compatibility checks         | CI-enforced                                            |
| Consumer inventory                    | Required for significant APIs                          |
| Deprecation                           | Defined migration + sunset                             |
| Contract testing                      | Required where consumer/provider independence warrants |
| Generated SDKs                        | Selective                                              |
| API catalog                           | Required at sufficient scale                           |
| Caching                               | Explicit + authorization-aware                         |
| ETag                                  | Supported                                              |
| API performance budgets               | Required for critical APIs                             |
| API ownership                         | Mandatory                                              |
| Status                                | **Accepted**                                           |
| Priority                              | **Critical**                                           |

---

---

# ADR-058 — Enterprise Frontend Architecture, React Platform, State Management, Design System, Web Performance & Frontend Security

## Part 2 — Sections 61–150

Continuing directly from **Section 60 — Performance Is an Architecture Requirement**.

---

# 61. Core Web Vitals

Mediverse should measure real user experience using Core Web Vitals and supporting frontend telemetry.

The primary dimensions are:

```text
LCP
→ Loading experience

INP
→ Interaction responsiveness

CLS
→ Visual stability
```

Synthetic tests alone are insufficient.

---

# 62. Largest Contentful Paint

LCP measures how quickly important visible content becomes available.

Typical contributors:

```text
Slow server response
Render-blocking resources
Large images
Large JavaScript bundles
Client-only data waterfalls
Fonts
```

Optimize the actual critical rendering path rather than chasing a score blindly.

---

# 63. Interaction to Next Paint

INP measures responsiveness to user interaction.

Poor INP may result from:

```text
Long JavaScript tasks
Heavy React rendering
Large DOM
Complex event handlers
Main-thread computation
Third-party scripts
```

---

# 64. Cumulative Layout Shift

Unexpected layout movement damages usability.

```text
Before:

[ Course title ]

After image loads:

[ IMAGE        ]
[ Course title ]
```

Reserve dimensions for images, video, 3D canvases and dynamically loaded content.

---

# 65. Real User Monitoring

Production performance should be measured from actual sessions.

```text
Browser
   │
   ▼
Performance Events
   │
   ▼
RUM
   │
   ▼
Metrics / Dashboards
```

RUM reveals device/network conditions that laboratory tests cannot fully reproduce.

---

# 66. Performance Budgets

Budgets should cover more than bundle size.

```text
JavaScript transfer
CSS
Images
Fonts
Third-party scripts
LCP
INP
CLS
API latency
```

CI should detect meaningful regressions.

---

# 67. Rendering Performance

Do not assume React rerenders are inherently problematic.

Optimize when measurement demonstrates meaningful cost.

```text
Measure
  │
  ▼
Identify bottleneck
  │
  ▼
Optimize
```

not:

```text
Memoize everything
```

---

# 68. Memoization

`memo`, `useMemo` and `useCallback` should be used deliberately.

They introduce their own complexity and runtime bookkeeping.

Use them when:

```text
Expensive computation exists
Referential stability matters
Measured rerender cost exists
```

---

# 69. Large Lists

Rendering thousands of DOM nodes simultaneously can degrade performance.

```text
10,000 records
     │
     ▼
Virtualized Window
     │
     ▼
Only visible rows rendered
```

Virtualization should be considered for genuinely large interactive collections.

---

# 70. Image Optimization

Educational imagery may become a major bandwidth cost.

Use:

```text
Appropriate dimensions
Responsive images
Modern formats
Lazy loading
Compression
CDN delivery
```

Do not ship a 5000×5000 anatomical image into a 300-pixel card.

---

# 71. Responsive Images

Browsers should receive appropriately sized assets.

Conceptually:

```html
<img
  srcset="small ... medium ... large ..."
  sizes="..."
>
```

This matters especially for mobile learners.

---

# 72. Video Architecture

Video should normally use specialized delivery rather than application-server file streaming.

```text
Source Video
    │
    ▼
Transcoding
    │
    ▼
Adaptive Streaming
    │
    ▼
CDN
    │
    ▼
Browser
```

Large media belongs in the media architecture established by earlier ADRs.

---

# 73. 3D Module Performance

Mediverse's 3D learning experiences require separate performance budgets.

```text
3D Scene
  │
  ├── Geometry
  ├── Textures
  ├── Materials
  ├── Lighting
  ├── Animation
  └── Physics
```

A visually impressive scene that destroys mobile performance is a failed educational feature.

---

# 74. 3D Asset Optimization

3D assets should be optimized using techniques appropriate to the rendering stack:

```text
Geometry simplification
Texture compression
LOD
Asset streaming
Instancing
Lazy loading
Efficient materials
```

Raw production-model assets should not automatically ship to browsers.

---

# 75. Level of Detail

Different model complexity may be used depending on distance or context.

```text
Far
→ Low detail

Medium
→ Medium detail

Close
→ High detail
```

LOD can substantially reduce GPU load.

---

# 76. WebGL Capability Detection

Do not assume every learner has a powerful GPU.

```text
Device Capability
       │
       ▼
Can support experience?
       │
   ┌───┴───┐
   ▼       ▼
  Yes      No
   │       │
   ▼       ▼
Full 3D   Reduced/Fallback Experience
```

Education must remain accessible when high-end rendering is unavailable.

---

# 77. Progressive 3D Enhancement

Core learning content should not become inaccessible solely because WebGL fails.

```text
Core Educational Content
        │
        ▼
Enhanced 3D Experience
```

3D should enhance learning rather than become an unnecessary availability dependency.

---

# 78. Web Workers

CPU-intensive browser operations may be moved away from the main thread.

```text
UI Thread
   │
   ▼
Worker
   │
   ▼
Heavy computation
```

Candidates may include parsing, transformation or computational workloads.

Workers do not directly manipulate the DOM.

---

# 79. Main Thread Budget

The browser main thread must remain responsive.

Avoid:

```text
Huge synchronous JSON processing
Expensive loops
Large DOM mutations
Heavy 3D calculations
Blocking third-party scripts
```

during critical interaction.

---

# 80. Browser Caching

Static assets should use effective caching.

```text
Hashed Asset
app.a81f3.js
     │
     ▼
Long Cache Lifetime
```

Content hashes permit aggressive immutable caching.

---

# 81. Service Workers

Service workers may enable:

```text
Offline caching
Background capabilities
Network interception
PWA behavior
```

They also introduce cache invalidation and deployment complexity.

Use them only with an explicit offline/PWA requirement.

---

# 82. PWA Decision

Mediverse may benefit from PWA capabilities where learners face inconsistent connectivity.

Potential value:

```text
Installability
Offline reading
Cached learning content
Reduced repeat bandwidth
```

But a PWA is not automatically required merely because Mediverse is a web application.

---

# 83. Offline Architecture

Offline support must define exactly what remains functional.

```text
Offline
 │
 ├── Previously downloaded chapter → YES
 ├── Cached images → MAYBE
 ├── New assessment submission → QUEUE?
 └── Live collaboration → NO
```

"Works offline" is too vague to implement.

---

# 84. Offline Mutations

Queuing state-changing operations offline introduces conflict problems.

```text
Offline Client
      │
      ▼
Mutation
      │
      ▼
Queue
      │
      ▼
Reconnect
      │
      ▼
Server state changed meanwhile?
```

Only workflows with clear reconciliation semantics should support this.

---

# 85. Realtime Frontend Integration

ADR-057 established WebSocket/SSE architecture.

Frontend real-time data should flow through a controlled abstraction.

```text
WebSocket / SSE
      │
      ▼
Realtime Client
      │
      ▼
Domain Event Handler
      │
      ▼
Query Cache / State
      │
      ▼
Components
```

Do not open unrelated socket connections from random components.

---

# 86. Realtime Cache Synchronization

Incoming events may:

```text
Invalidate query
Update cached entity
Append notification
Trigger refetch
```

The strategy depends on domain semantics.

---

# 87. Reconnection State

After reconnection:

```text
Connection Lost
      │
      ▼
Events missed
      │
      ▼
Reconnect
      │
      ▼
Resynchronize authoritative state
```

Do not assume no events occurred during disconnection.

---

# 88. Accessibility

Accessibility is a product requirement, not optional polish.

Mediverse should target an appropriate **WCAG 2.x AA-level** standard for applicable experiences.

---

# 89. Semantic HTML

Prefer native semantic elements.

```html
<button>
<nav>
<main>
<form>
<label>
```

over rebuilding basic semantics from generic `<div>` elements.

Native semantics provide accessibility behavior for free.

---

# 90. Keyboard Navigation

All critical functionality should be operable without a mouse.

Test:

```text
Tab
Shift+Tab
Enter
Space
Escape
Arrow navigation where appropriate
```

---

# 91. Focus Management

Dynamic interfaces must manage focus deliberately.

Examples:

```text
Modal opens
→ Focus moves appropriately

Modal closes
→ Focus returns appropriately

Route changes
→ Page context remains understandable
```

---

# 92. Screen Readers

Interactive controls need meaningful accessible names and relationships.

Do not create:

```html
<div onclick="...">X</div>
```

when a semantic button is appropriate.

---

# 93. ARIA

ARIA should supplement semantic HTML.

Rule:

> Prefer native semantics before adding ARIA.

Incorrect ARIA can make accessibility worse.

---

# 94. Accessible Forms

Forms require:

```text
Labels
Instructions
Error association
Keyboard operation
Focus handling
Required-state communication
```

Color alone must not communicate errors.

---

# 95. Color Contrast

Text and interactive elements should meet required contrast targets.

The design system should encode accessible combinations instead of forcing every developer to calculate them independently.

---

# 96. Reduced Motion

Users may request reduced motion.

```text
prefers-reduced-motion
```

should influence animations where appropriate.

This is particularly relevant to immersive 3D experiences.

---

# 97. Accessibility Testing

Use multiple layers:

```text
Static rules
Automated accessibility tests
Component tests
Browser tests
Manual keyboard testing
Screen-reader validation for critical workflows
```

Automated tools cannot prove full accessibility.

---

# 98. Responsive Architecture

Mediverse should be mobile-first.

```text
Mobile
  │
  ▼
Tablet
  │
  ▼
Desktop
  │
  ▼
Large Display
```

Do not build desktop first and then hide half the interface on phones.

---

# 99. Breakpoints

Breakpoints should follow layout requirements rather than specific device brands.

```text
Content no longer fits
      │
      ▼
Layout changes
```

This is more durable than designing for individual phone models.

---

# 100. Touch Interaction

Interactive targets should be practical for touch input.

Hover-only functionality is unacceptable for essential workflows.

---

# 101. Design System

Mediverse should establish a governed design system.

```text
Design Tokens
      │
      ▼
Primitives
      │
      ▼
Components
      │
      ▼
Patterns
      │
      ▼
Product Features
```

This provides consistency without duplicating UI logic.

---

# 102. Design Tokens

Tokens should represent foundational decisions.

```text
Typography
Spacing
Radius
Elevation
Color
Motion
Breakpoints
```

Feature code should avoid arbitrary repeated values where tokens exist.

---

# 103. Semantic Tokens

Prefer semantic meaning:

```text
color.text.primary
color.surface.error
color.action.primary
```

over application-wide dependencies on raw values such as:

```text
#1976d2
```

Semantic tokens make themes and redesigns easier.

---

# 104. Component Library

Reusable components may include:

```text
Button
Input
Select
Dialog
Card
Table
Tabs
Tooltip
Navigation
Feedback
```

But do not build custom versions of mature primitives merely to claim Mediverse has its own design system.

---

# 105. MUI Boundary

MUI may provide the foundational component layer.

```text
MUI
 │
 ▼
Mediverse Design Components
 │
 ▼
Features
```

Feature code should preferably consume Mediverse-governed abstractions for highly standardized components.

---

# 106. Tailwind Boundary

If Tailwind is retained, its role must be explicit.

A reasonable boundary is:

```text
Tailwind
→ Layout / utility styling

MUI / Design System
→ Complex interactive components
```

Using MUI, Tailwind and arbitrary CSS simultaneously without rules creates visual and maintenance inconsistency.

---

# 107. Styling Governance

Reject:

```text
MUI sx
+
Tailwind
+
CSS Modules
+
Styled Components
+
inline style
+
global CSS
```

all used randomly for identical concerns.

Select a small, documented styling strategy.

---

# 108. Storybook

Storybook should be considered for isolated development and documentation of reusable design-system components.

```text
Component
   │
   ├── Variants
   ├── States
   ├── Accessibility
   └── Documentation
```

It becomes especially valuable as component ownership grows.

---

# 109. Theming

Theme configuration should centrally control:

```text
Colors
Typography
Spacing
Component defaults
Motion
```

Features should not implement independent theme systems.

---

# 110. Dark Mode

Dark mode should be token-driven.

```text
Semantic Token
     │
     ├── Light Theme
     └── Dark Theme
```

Do not implement dark mode as hundreds of conditional component styles.

---

# 111. Internationalization

User-visible strings should be externalizable where multilingual support is required.

```text
Component
   │
   ▼
Translation Key
   │
   ▼
Locale Resource
```

Avoid hardcoding user-facing text throughout components.

---

# 112. Translation Is More Than String Replacement

Languages differ in:

```text
Word length
Grammar
Pluralization
Ordering
Gender
Number formatting
Date formatting
Direction
```

UI layouts must tolerate these differences.

---

# 113. Pluralization

Do not construct translated phrases using naive concatenation.

```text
count + " students"
```

Localization frameworks should handle plural rules.

---

# 114. RTL

If right-to-left languages become supported:

```text
LTR
◄────────────►
RTL
◄────────────►
```

layout, icons, navigation and spacing must be evaluated.

Logical CSS properties can reduce hardcoded directional assumptions.

---

# 115. Date and Time

Store/communicate timestamps using unambiguous formats.

Presentation should consider:

```text
User locale
User timezone
Course timezone
Event timezone
```

Never assume the browser's timezone represents the business timezone for every workflow.

---

# 116. Frontend Observability

Production frontend telemetry should cover:

```text
JavaScript errors
Unhandled promise rejections
API failures
Web Vitals
Route performance
Resource failures
Release version
Device/browser context
```

while respecting privacy constraints.

---

# 117. Error Monitoring

Errors should include enough context to diagnose failures:

```text
Release
Route
Error
Stack
Correlation ID
Relevant feature
```

Avoid capturing unnecessary sensitive data.

---

# 118. Source Maps

Production source maps are valuable for debugging minified errors.

They should be managed so diagnostic systems can use them without unnecessarily exposing source internals publicly.

---

# 119. Correlation IDs

Frontend error reports should include backend correlation/trace identifiers where available.

```text
Browser Error
     │
     ▼
Request ID
     │
     ▼
Gateway
     │
     ▼
Backend Trace
```

This connects user-visible failures with distributed-system diagnostics.

---

# 120. Analytics

Product analytics should answer defined questions.

Examples:

```text
Course completion
Feature adoption
Navigation friction
Assessment abandonment
```

Do not collect every possible interaction merely because analytics tooling permits it.

---

# 121. Privacy-Aware Telemetry

Telemetry must avoid accidental capture of:

```text
Passwords
Tokens
Sensitive form fields
Private learning content
Personal data beyond approved purpose
```

Logging every Redux state transition to production analytics would be reckless.

---

# 122. Content Security Policy

CSP should restrict where executable/browser resources can originate.

Conceptually:

```text
script-src
style-src
img-src
connect-src
frame-src
```

CSP provides defense in depth against classes of content injection.

---

# 123. XSS

Cross-site scripting remains a critical browser threat.

React escapes ordinary rendered strings by default, but unsafe APIs can bypass that protection.

---

# 124. Dangerous HTML

Use of:

```text
dangerouslySetInnerHTML
```

requires explicit justification.

Untrusted HTML must be sanitized using a proven sanitization approach.

Do not write a custom regex HTML sanitizer.

---

# 125. Rich Educational Content

Mediverse may render rich medical content.

The trust boundary should be:

```text
Content Source
     │
     ▼
Validation / Sanitization
     │
     ▼
Approved Renderer
     │
     ▼
Browser
```

CMS/editor content should not automatically be considered safe HTML.

---

# 126. Trusted Types

Trusted Types should be evaluated for high-security browser deployments where the application/browser support model makes it practical.

It can strengthen DOM-XSS defenses but does not replace secure coding.

---

# 127. CSRF

If Mediverse uses cookie-based authentication:

```text
Browser Cookie
     │
     ▼
State-changing API
```

CSRF protections from ADR-056/057 remain required.

Frontend and backend architecture must agree on the mechanism.

---

# 128. Clickjacking

Sensitive Mediverse interfaces should control whether they can be embedded by external sites.

Use appropriate browser security headers/policies.

Do not rely on JavaScript frame-busting hacks.

---

# 129. Dependency Security

The frontend dependency tree is a supply-chain boundary.

```text
Application
   │
   ▼
Direct Dependencies
   │
   ▼
Transitive Dependencies
```

One compromised package can affect the shipped browser application.

---

# 130. Lockfiles

Package lockfiles should be committed and respected by CI.

```text
package.json
     +
lockfile
     │
     ▼
Reproducible Dependency Graph
```

Uncontrolled dependency resolution damages reproducibility.

---

# 131. Dependency Updates

Dependencies should be updated deliberately.

Avoid both extremes:

```text
Never update anything
```

and:

```text
Automatically merge every major upgrade into production
```

Security, compatibility and regression testing must guide updates.

---

# 132. Third-Party Scripts

Every third-party browser script executes inside a high-value trust boundary.

Examples:

```text
Analytics
Chat widgets
Advertising
Monitoring
Payment integrations
```

Minimize them.

Evaluate:

```text
Security
Privacy
Performance
Availability
Business necessity
```

before inclusion.

---

# 133. Feature Flags

Feature flags decouple deployment from release.

```text
Deploy Code
    │
    ▼
Feature OFF
    │
    ▼
Controlled Enablement
```

They can support gradual rollout and emergency disablement.

---

# 134. Flag Types

Differentiate:

```text
Release flags
Experiment flags
Operational flags
Permission/entitlement configuration
```

Do not use frontend feature flags as authorization.

---

# 135. Flag Lifecycle

Temporary flags must have owners and removal dates.

Otherwise:

```text
if flagA
  if flagB
    if !flagC
```

eventually becomes permanent architectural debt.

---

# 136. Frontend Testing Pyramid

A healthy strategy combines:

```text
           E2E
          /   \
     Integration
       /       \
   Component / Unit
```

Do not attempt to prove the entire application using thousands of brittle browser tests.

---

# 137. Vitest

Vitest should be used for fast unit-level testing in the Vite ecosystem where appropriate.

Targets include:

```text
Utilities
Reducers
Hooks
Domain transformations
Validation
```

---

# 138. React Testing Library

Component tests should focus on user-observable behavior.

Prefer:

```text
User clicks Submit
Error message appears
```

over testing internal component implementation details.

---

# 139. MSW

Mock Service Worker should be evaluated for realistic API mocking in frontend tests and development.

```text
Frontend
   │
   ▼
HTTP Request
   │
   ▼
MSW
   │
   ▼
Contract-aligned Response
```

Mocks must remain synchronized with API contracts.

---

# 140. Playwright

Playwright should cover critical end-to-end workflows.

Examples:

```text
Login
Course enrollment
Chapter learning
Assessment submission
Instructor workflow
Critical administration
```

Focus on business-critical journeys.

---

# 141. Visual Regression

Design-system and high-value screens may use screenshot-based regression testing.

This can detect:

```text
Layout breakage
Theme regression
Unexpected component changes
Responsive failures
```

Visual tests require controlled environments to avoid noise.

---

# 142. Accessibility CI

Automated accessibility checks should run against critical components/pages.

They supplement—not replace—manual accessibility validation.

---

# 143. Frontend Contract Testing

Frontend CI should validate compatibility against ADR-057 API contracts.

```text
OpenAPI
   │
   ▼
Generated Types / Client
   │
   ▼
Compile
   │
   ▼
Contract Tests
```

Backend contract changes should fail early when they break frontend assumptions.

---

# 144. Frontend CI/CD

Conceptually:

```text
Commit
  │
  ▼
Lint
  │
  ▼
Type Check
  │
  ▼
Unit / Component Tests
  │
  ▼
Accessibility Checks
  │
  ▼
Build
  │
  ▼
Bundle Budget
  │
  ▼
Security Scan
  │
  ▼
E2E / Smoke
  │
  ▼
Immutable Artifact
  │
  ▼
Deploy
```

The same artifact should move through environments where feasible.

---

# 145. Static Asset Deployment

Production React assets should typically follow:

```text
Build
  │
  ▼
Immutable Static Assets
  │
  ▼
Object/Static Hosting
  │
  ▼
CDN
  │
  ▼
Browser
```

Application servers should not unnecessarily serve large static bundles when dedicated infrastructure exists.

---

# 146. Cache Busting & Rollback

Hashed filenames enable simultaneous old/new assets.

```text
app.a123.js
app.b456.js
```

Deployment must avoid HTML referencing assets that no longer exist.

Rollback should restore a coherent artifact set rather than reconstructing builds manually.

---

# 147. Micro-Frontend Decision

Mediverse should **not adopt micro-frontends by default**.

They become justified when there is a real organizational problem such as:

```text
Multiple autonomous frontend teams
Independent release requirements
Clearly separated domains
Different deployment cadences
```

A large application is not automatically a micro-frontend problem.

---

# 148. Micro-Frontend Trade-Offs

Micro-frontends can provide:

```text
Team autonomy
Independent delivery
Domain ownership
```

but introduce:

```text
Duplicate dependencies
Inconsistent UX
Runtime integration complexity
Routing complexity
Shared-state problems
Version conflicts
Observability complexity
Performance overhead
```

Module Federation or similar technology should only follow an explicit architectural decision.

---

# 149. Frontend Anti-Patterns

Mediverse rejects:

```text
❌ JavaScript for large production code where TypeScript is practical
❌ any everywhere
❌ Technical-folder-only architecture at application scale
❌ shared/ as a dumping ground
❌ Arbitrary cross-feature deep imports
❌ 2,000-line page components containing entire domains
❌ Redux for every piece of state
❌ Server responses copied blindly into Redux
❌ Every state value stored globally
❌ Derived values duplicated in state
❌ API calls scattered through random components
❌ Client validation trusted as security
❌ React route guards treated as authorization
❌ Long-lived sensitive tokens casually stored in localStorage
❌ Secrets embedded in Vite environment variables
❌ One global loading spinner for every operation
❌ Memoization everywhere without measurement
❌ Entire application shipped as one giant bundle
❌ Raw high-resolution images sent to tiny displays
❌ Unoptimized 3D assets shipped directly to mobile browsers
❌ 3D rendering made mandatory for basic educational access
❌ Unlimited DOM lists
❌ Service worker introduced without cache lifecycle design
❌ "Offline support" without defined semantics
❌ Socket connections created by random components
❌ Reconnect loops without backoff
❌ Mouse-only interaction
❌ div-based fake buttons
❌ Accessibility postponed until launch
❌ Desktop-only design followed by emergency mobile fixes
❌ MUI + Tailwind + CSS-in-JS + global CSS used randomly
❌ Hardcoded colors instead of design tokens
❌ User-facing strings hardcoded everywhere
❌ Browser timezone assumed to equal business timezone
❌ Sensitive values captured in analytics
❌ Unsanitized HTML rendering
❌ Custom regex HTML sanitizers
❌ Uncontrolled third-party scripts
❌ Feature flags used as authorization
❌ Permanent abandoned feature flags
❌ Testing implementation details instead of behavior
❌ Entire test strategy dependent on E2E
❌ Mutable production frontend artifacts
❌ Micro-frontends introduced because they sound enterprise
```

---

# 150. Decision Outcome & Final Reference Architecture

| Area                        | Decision                                        |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Framework                   | **React**                                       |
| Language                    | **TypeScript**                                  |
| Build platform              | **Vite**                                        |
| Code organization           | Domain/feature-oriented                         |
| Feature interfaces          | Controlled public exports                       |
| Routing                     | React Router                                    |
| Route guards                | UX only                                         |
| Local state                 | React                                           |
| URL state                   | Router/URL                                      |
| Server state                | TanStack Query preferred where appropriate      |
| Global complex client state | Redux Toolkit selectively                       |
| Form architecture           | React Hook Form                                 |
| Runtime schema validation   | Required where appropriate                      |
| API access                  | Feature API layer + shared HTTP client          |
| Generated OpenAPI client    | Preferred/evaluated                             |
| Browser authentication      | ADR-056 governed                                |
| BFF                         | Preferred evaluation for sensitive browser auth |
| Browser secrets             | **Impossible by design — do not embed**         |
| Error isolation             | React Error Boundaries                          |
| Code splitting              | Route/feature based                             |
| 3D modules                  | Lazy-loaded + separately budgeted               |
| Performance                 | Core Web Vitals + RUM                           |
| Large lists                 | Virtualization when needed                      |
| Images                      | Responsive + optimized + CDN                    |
| 3D                          | Progressive enhancement                         |
| PWA                         | Requirement-driven                              |
| Offline                     | Explicit capability model                       |
| Realtime                    | Central client abstraction                      |
| Accessibility               | WCAG 2.x AA target                              |
| Responsive design           | Mobile-first                                    |
| Design system               | Required                                        |
| UI foundation               | MUI                                             |
| Tailwind                    | Controlled utility/layout role                  |
| Storybook                   | Design-system documentation/testing             |
| Theme                       | Token-driven                                    |
| Dark mode                   | Semantic-token based                            |
| i18n                        | Architecture-supported                          |
| Time handling               | Locale + timezone aware                         |
| Frontend observability      | Required                                        |
| Source maps                 | Controlled diagnostic access                    |
| CSP                         | Required defense-in-depth                       |
| Untrusted HTML              | Sanitized                                       |
| Dependency lockfile         | Required                                        |
| Supply-chain scanning       | CI enforced                                     |
| Feature flags               | Lifecycle-governed                              |
| Unit testing                | Vitest                                          |
| Component testing           | React Testing Library                           |
| API mocking                 | MSW                                             |
| E2E                         | Playwright                                      |
| Accessibility CI            | Required                                        |
| Visual regression           | Critical UI/design system                       |
| API contract validation     | Required                                        |
| Artifact                    | Immutable                                       |
| Static deployment           | CDN-oriented                                    |
| Rollback                    | Previous immutable artifact                     |
| Micro-frontends             | **Rejected as default**                         |
| Module Federation           | Only after explicit justification               |
| Status                      | **Accepted**                                    |
| Priority                    | **Critical**                                    |

## ADR-058 — COMPLETE ✅

The resulting Mediverse frontend architecture is:

```text
                              USER
                               │
                               ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────┐
                    │      BROWSER        │
                    │  Mobile / Desktop   │
                    └──────────┬──────────┘

                         CDN / EDGE

                    │   REACT + TS APP    │
                    └──────────┬──────────┘
                               │
            ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐
            ▼                  ▼                  ▼
         ROUTING           DESIGN SYSTEM       FEATURES
            │                                     │
            │           ┌─────────────────────────┼──────────────┐
            │           ▼            ▼            ▼              ▼
            │        Courses      Learning    Assessment       Admin
            │           │            │            │              │
            └───────────┴────────────┴────────────┴──────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
                         STATE MODEL
                               │
          ┌────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐
          ▼                    ▼                     ▼
       LOCAL/UI            SERVER STATE          GLOBAL
        React             TanStack Query       Redux Toolkit
          │                    │                     │
          └────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘
                               ▼
                        FEATURE API LAYER
                               │

                               │

                  ───── REAL-TIME PLANE ─────

                  WebSocket / SSE
                         │

          Accessibility ─ Design System ─ Responsive
                │              │              │

                               ▼

                               │
                    Progressive Enhancement

                   ───── SECURITY PLANE ─────

             CSP ─ XSS Defense ─ CSRF Controls
              │         │             │

                        ▼
                Supply-Chain Controls

                 ───── QUALITY PLANE ─────

       TypeCheck → Vitest → RTL → Accessibility
                         │
                         ▼

                         │

                   Bundle Budgets

              ───── OBSERVABILITY PLANE ─────
```

The frontend has one final invariant:

> **A feature is not production-ready merely because it renders correctly on the developer's machine. It must remain secure, accessible, responsive, observable, contract-compatible, performant on realistic devices, testable, and safely deployable.**


### **ADR-059 — Enterprise Mobile Architecture, React Native, Offline-First Learning, Synchronization, Push Notifications, Mobile Security & App Delivery**

ADR-059 should cover **mobile platform strategy → native vs React Native vs PWA → shared web/mobile boundaries → React Native architecture → Expo evaluation → TypeScript → navigation → mobile feature modules → API client reuse → authentication → OAuth/OIDC native flows → PKCE → secure token storage → biometric authentication → Keychain/Keystore → certificate/network security → device integrity considerations → local database → SQLite → encrypted storage → offline-first learning → downloadable courses → media downloads → 3D mobile constraints → synchronization engine → dirty tracking → sync queue → conflict detection → conflict resolution → optimistic mutations → idempotency → retry/backoff → delta synchronization → background synchronization → network awareness → push notifications → FCM/APNs → notification permissions → deep links → universal/app links → notification security → mobile state management → caching → image/media optimization → battery/data usage → accessibility → responsive device layouts → tablet experience → localization → mobile analytics → crash reporting → privacy → mobile secrets → API keys → root/jailbreak threat model → screenshot/clipboard considerations → testing → unit/component/E2E → device matrix → performance testing → release signing → Android/iOS builds → CI/CD → Play Store/App Store → staged rollout → feature flags → forced/minimum versions → backward API compatibility → OTA update boundaries → rollback → observability → mobile SLOs → anti-patterns → final Mediverse enterprise mobile/offline architecture.**

# ADR-059 — Enterprise Mobile Architecture

## Part 2 — Sections 61–150

Continuing directly from **Section 60 — Notes Synchronization**.

---

# 61. Delta Synchronization

Mobile clients should not repeatedly download complete datasets merely to discover a few changes.

Prefer:

```text
Device
  │
  │ lastSyncCursor = abc123
  ▼
Server
  │
  ▼
Changes since abc123
  │
  ├── Updated entities
  ├── New entities
  └── Deleted entities
```

Delta synchronization reduces bandwidth, processing and battery consumption.

---

# 62. Sync Cursor

The server may issue an opaque synchronization cursor.

```text
GET /sync?cursor=abc123

Response
├── changes[]
└── nextCursor=xyz789
```

Clients must treat cursors as opaque tokens rather than attempting to interpret their internal structure.

---

# 63. Cursor Consistency

A cursor should represent a meaningful server-side synchronization position.

It should not simply be:

```text
client current timestamp
```

when clock differences or concurrent writes can cause missed records.

---

# 64. Sync Pagination

Large synchronization results should be paginated.

```text
cursor=A
   │
   ▼
Page 1
   │
   ▼
continuation=B
   │
   ▼
Page 2
```

The client should advance its durable synchronization checkpoint only according to defined consistency semantics.

---

# 65. Deletions

Delta synchronization must communicate deletions.

Otherwise:

```text
Server deletes Course X

Device never receives Course X again

But local Course X remains forever
```

This creates stale local state.

---

# 66. Tombstones

A deletion may temporarily be represented by a tombstone.

```text
{
   id: "course-123",
   deleted: true,
   version: 17
}
```

Tombstones allow offline clients to learn that previously synchronized records were removed.

---

# 67. Tombstone Retention

Tombstones cannot necessarily be retained forever.

Therefore the synchronization architecture needs a retention policy.

If a device has been offline beyond the supported synchronization window:

```text
Incremental Sync
      │
      X
Cursor expired
      │
      ▼
Full Resynchronization
```

may be required.

---

# 68. Multi-Device Synchronization

A learner may use:

```text
Phone
Tablet
Web
```

against the same account.

The server remains authoritative for shared state.

```text
Phone ──┐
Tablet ─┼──► Server State
Web ────┘
```

Do not design synchronization assuming one user owns one device.

---

# 69. Device Identity

A generated installation/device identifier may help with:

```text
Push registration
Sync diagnostics
Session management
Conflict analysis
```

It must not be treated as proof of user identity.

---

# 70. Background Synchronization

Where OS capabilities permit:

```text
Application Backgrounded
        │
        ▼
OS grants execution window
        │
        ▼
Sync Engine
        │
        ▼
Upload/download limited changes
```

Background execution must be considered opportunistic.

---

# 71. OS Background Restrictions

This assumption is rejected:

```text
Background worker
      =
Runs whenever we want
```

Android and iOS aggressively manage background execution.

Critical workflows must not depend on unrestricted background processing.

---

# 72. Foreground Synchronization

When the application returns to foreground:

```text
App Resume
   │
   ▼
Check freshness
   │
   ▼
Sync if necessary
```

This is an important recovery mechanism when background execution did not occur.

---

# 73. Connectivity Detection

Network APIs can indicate connectivity state.

But:

```text
Connected to Wi-Fi
       ≠
Mediverse API reachable
```

Actual request outcomes remain authoritative.

---

# 74. Network State

Useful states include:

```text
Offline
Wi-Fi
Cellular
Unknown
Expensive connection
```

The application may adapt synchronization and download behavior accordingly.

---

# 75. Push Notification Architecture

Push notifications should use platform push services.

```text
Mediverse
    │
    ▼
Notification Service
    │
    ├───────────────┐
    ▼               ▼
   FCM             APNs
    │               │
    ▼               ▼
 Android           iOS
```

Mediverse should not attempt to maintain persistent connections solely to reinvent platform push delivery.

---

# 76. Push Tokens

Platform push tokens identify application installations/endpoints.

```text
User
 │
 ├── Phone token A
 ├── Tablet token B
 └── Old token C
```

They are mutable infrastructure identifiers, not permanent user IDs.

---

# 77. Push Token Lifecycle

Tokens may:

```text
Rotate
Expire
Become invalid
Change after reinstall
```

The backend must update registrations and remove invalid tokens.

---

# 78. User-to-Device Mapping

Push registration should associate:

```text
User
Installation
Platform
Push token
Application version
Notification preferences
```

where required.

Logout/account switching must update this association correctly.

---

# 79. Notification Preferences

Users should control supported categories such as:

```text
Learning reminders
Course updates
Assessment reminders
Social/activity notifications
Announcements
```

Transactional or mandatory notifications should be classified separately where applicable.

---

# 80. Notification Permission

Push permission should be requested contextually.

Bad:

```text
First app launch
      │
      ▼
Immediately request every permission
```

Better:

```text
User understands feature
      │
      ▼
Explain value
      │
      ▼
Request required permission
```

---

# 81. Push Payload Security

Push payloads should contain the minimum information necessary.

Do not assume push infrastructure or the lock screen is an appropriate place for sensitive data.

Prefer:

```text
"New learning update available"
```

over exposing sensitive educational/account information unnecessarily.

---

# 82. Push Is a Signal

Where freshness matters:

```text
Push
 │
 ▼
Application
 │
 ▼
Fetch authoritative state
```

The push message should not necessarily become the authoritative domain record.

---

# 83. Notification Deep Links

A notification may route to:

```text
Course
Chapter
Assessment
Message
Announcement
```

but destination authorization remains mandatory.

---

# 84. Notification Deduplication

Retries or multiple event paths can produce duplicates.

Use stable notification/event identifiers where necessary.

```text
eventId
   │
   ▼
Already processed?
   │
 ┌─┴─┐
 ▼   ▼
Yes  No
 │    │
Drop Process
```

---

# 85. Local Notifications

The mobile application may schedule local reminders for suitable workflows.

Example:

```text
Study reminder
Downloaded assessment reminder
```

Local notifications should not represent server-authoritative events that require fresh server state.

---

# 86. Badge State

Badge counts require explicit semantics.

```text
Unread notifications?
Unread messages?
Pending tasks?
```

Do not mix unrelated concepts into an unexplained number.

---

# 87. Mobile State Architecture

ADR-058 principles remain applicable:

```text
Local UI State
→ React

Server State
→ TanStack Query where appropriate

Complex Global Client State
→ Redux Toolkit selectively

Persistent Offline State
→ Local database

Navigation State
→ Navigation system
```

---

# 88. Local Database Is Not Redux

This architecture is rejected:

```text
SQLite
  │
  ▼
Copy everything
  │
  ▼
Redux
```

Duplicating large persistent datasets creates synchronization and memory problems.

---

# 89. TanStack Query Mobile

TanStack Query may manage online server-state caching.

It must integrate carefully with:

```text
Connectivity
App foreground/background
Persistent storage
Offline database
Sync engine
```

Do not create two competing authoritative caches.

---

# 90. Memory Pressure

Mobile memory is constrained.

Avoid retaining:

```text
Huge course datasets
Decoded full-resolution images
Multiple 3D scenes
Large video buffers
Unbounded query caches
```

simultaneously.

---

# 91. Image Cache

Images may use a managed cache.

```text
Remote Image
    │
    ▼
Disk Cache
    │
    ▼
Decoded Image
    │
    ▼
Screen
```

Memory and disk caching require separate limits.

---

# 92. Media Cache

Streaming media cache and explicitly downloaded media should be distinguished.

```text
Temporary playback cache
        ≠
User-selected offline download
```

Eviction policies should respect that distinction.

---

# 93. Battery Efficiency

Mobile architecture should minimize:

```text
Continuous polling
Unnecessary GPS
Repeated wakeups
Aggressive background synchronization
Constant socket reconnects
Excessive animation
Unnecessary 3D rendering
```

Battery consumption is an application-quality metric.

---

# 94. Bandwidth Budget

Mediverse should measure:

```text
Cold-start traffic
Normal session traffic
Course download size
Image transfer
Video transfer
Synchronization traffic
```

Mobile bandwidth is not unlimited.

---

# 95. Accessibility

Mobile accessibility remains mandatory.

Support should include:

```text
Screen readers
Dynamic text sizing
Accessible labels
Touch target sizing
Focus order
Contrast
Reduced motion
```

---

# 96. Dynamic Type

Interfaces should tolerate larger system font settings.

This is unacceptable:

```text
Larger font
   │
   ▼
Text clipped
Buttons inaccessible
Navigation broken
```

Layouts should adapt.

---

# 97. Screen Readers

Important elements require meaningful accessibility semantics for technologies such as platform screen readers.

Icon-only controls require accessible labels.

---

# 98. Touch Targets

Interactive elements should provide practical touch areas.

Tiny visual icons should not require pixel-perfect tapping.

---

# 99. Orientation

Do not assume portrait-only unless the product explicitly requires it.

3D anatomical learning and tablet workflows may benefit significantly from landscape layouts.

---

# 100. Tablet Architecture

Tablet should not simply be:

```text
Phone UI stretched to 13 inches
```

Large displays may support:

```text
Master/detail
Split panes
Persistent navigation
Side-by-side learning material
3D + explanation panels
```

---

# 101. Foldables and Variable Windows

Responsive layout decisions should depend on available window dimensions rather than rigid assumptions about device categories.

---

# 102. Localization

Mobile follows the internationalization architecture established in ADR-058.

Support should include:

```text
Translation
Pluralization
Number formatting
Dates
Time zones
RTL
Locale-aware content
```

---

# 103. Mobile Observability

Production mobile telemetry should capture approved signals such as:

```text
Crashes
Unhandled errors
Application hangs
Startup performance
API failures
Sync failures
Release version
Device/OS class
Navigation failures
```

while respecting privacy controls.

---

# 104. Crash Reporting

Crash reports should identify:

```text
App version
Build number
OS version
Device class
Stack trace
Release
Relevant breadcrumbs
```

without unnecessarily collecting sensitive user content.

---

# 105. ANR / Application Hangs

Crash-free statistics alone are insufficient.

An application that freezes for 20 seconds but does not crash still provides a failed experience.

Monitor:

```text
Android ANRs
iOS hangs
Long JS-thread stalls
```

where tooling permits.

---

# 106. Startup Performance

Measure:

```text
Process start
    │
    ▼
Application shell
    │
    ▼
Usable screen
```

Do not initialize every SDK, course cache and analytics subsystem before showing useful UI.

---

# 107. Lazy Initialization

Non-critical capabilities should initialize when needed.

Candidates:

```text
3D engine
Heavy analytics
Rare admin capabilities
Large editors
Optional integrations
```

---

# 108. Frame Rate

Animations, scrolling and 3D interactions should remain responsive on supported devices.

Monitor dropped frames rather than assuming development-machine performance represents production devices.

---

# 109. JavaScript Thread

React Native workloads must avoid monopolizing the JS thread with expensive synchronous processing.

Heavy work should be restructured, deferred or moved to suitable native/background mechanisms where justified.

---

# 110. Memory Monitoring

Memory-heavy workflows require testing:

```text
Large course
+
Video
+
Images
+
3D model
+
Navigation history
```

Memory leaks may cause operating-system termination rather than clean application errors.

---

# 111. Analytics & Privacy

Mobile analytics should have defined purposes.

Collect:

```text
What product decision will this event support?
```

before adding telemetry.

Avoid indiscriminate event collection.

---

# 112. Mobile Secrets

An APK or IPA cannot securely hide static secrets.

Reject:

```text
Secret API key
      │
      ▼
Bundle into app
      │
      ▼
"Nobody will find it"
```

Anything distributed to clients should be treated as extractable.

---

# 113. TLS

All production network communication containing protected application traffic should use HTTPS/TLS.

The mobile client must validate server certificates correctly.

---

# 114. Certificate Pinning

Certificate pinning can reduce some interception risks but introduces operational hazards:

```text
Certificate rotation
Emergency changes
CDN migration
Pin expiration
Application versions unable to update
```

Therefore Mediverse should **not adopt certificate pinning by default**.

Use it only after explicit threat-model justification and with a safe rotation strategy.

---

# 115. Rooted/Jailbroken Devices

Root/jailbreak detection can provide a risk signal.

It is not a reliable security boundary.

```text
Device detection
      │
      ▼
Risk signal
      │
      X
Absolute proof
```

Server-side authorization and security controls remain mandatory.

---

# 116. Device Attestation

Platform attestation mechanisms may be evaluated for high-risk capabilities.

Potential use:

```text
App installation
      │
      ▼
Platform Attestation
      │
      ▼
Risk Engine
```

Attestation should contribute to risk decisions rather than replace authentication.

---

# 117. Screenshots

Sensitive screens may require screenshot/screen-recording restrictions where platform capabilities and threat models justify them.

Do not apply restrictions indiscriminately; they can harm legitimate accessibility and learning workflows.

---

# 118. Clipboard

Sensitive data should not automatically be copied into the system clipboard.

Clipboard contents may be accessible beyond the immediate application context depending on platform behavior.

---

# 119. Application Backups

Sensitive local data must be evaluated against Android/iOS backup behavior.

Data that should not leave the device through platform backup mechanisms must be configured accordingly.

---

# 120. Android Exported Components

Android activities/services/receivers/providers should follow least exposure.

```text
Does another application need access?
        │
   ┌────┴────┐
   ▼         ▼
  Yes        No
   │         │
Explicit   Not exported
control
```

---

# 121. Intent Validation

External Android intents and deep-link parameters are untrusted input.

Validate them before use.

---

# 122. iOS URL Handling

Incoming URLs/universal links should also be treated as untrusted navigation input.

Malformed or unauthorized routes must fail safely.

---

# 123. WebView Security

WebViews should be minimized.

When required:

```text
Trusted origins
Navigation restrictions
Controlled JavaScript
Secure bridge design
No unnecessary file access
```

must be defined.

A WebView JavaScript bridge can become a serious security boundary.

---

# 124. Permissions

Request only permissions required by real features.

```text
Camera
Microphone
Photos
Notifications
Location
```

should each have explicit product justification.

Mediverse should not request location merely because a dependency supports it.

---

# 125. Permission Timing

Permissions should be requested near the feature that needs them.

Context improves user understanding and reduces unnecessary permission denial.

---

# 126. Native Dependency Security

React Native applications include:

```text
npm packages
Native Android dependencies
Native iOS dependencies
Build plugins
Expo/native modules
```

Supply-chain scanning must account for all layers.

---

# 127. Testing Strategy

Mobile quality requires:

```text
Unit tests
Component tests
Integration tests
E2E tests
Offline tests
Migration tests
Real-device tests
Performance tests
```

One emulator is not a mobile testing strategy.

---

# 128. Unit & Component Tests

Test:

```text
Domain transformations
Sync state machines
Conflict rules
Validation
Hooks
UI behavior
```

without requiring full-device execution where unnecessary.

---

# 129. Sync Engine Testing

Synchronization deserves dedicated deterministic tests.

Test scenarios including:

```text
Successful sync
Network failure
Timeout
Duplicate request
Server conflict
Cursor expiration
Partial synchronization
Application termination
Retry
Deletion/tombstone
```

---

# 130. Offline Testing

Explicitly test:

```text
Launch offline
Lose network during operation
Reconnect
Switch Wi-Fi → cellular
Slow connection
High latency
Packet loss
API unavailable
```

Offline-first architecture cannot be validated only on stable office Wi-Fi.

---

# 131. Database Migration Testing

Test upgrades across supported historical versions.

```text
App v8 DB
   │
   ▼
Upgrade directly to v12
```

may be a real user path.

Testing only fresh installs misses migration failures.

---

# 132. Device Matrix

Testing should cover representative:

```text
Low-end Android
Mid-range Android
High-end Android
Supported iPhones
Tablet
Different OS versions
Different screen dimensions
```

The exact matrix should derive from supported-user telemetry.

---

# 133. Physical Devices

Emulators/simulators are valuable but cannot fully reproduce:

```text
GPU behavior
Camera
Biometrics
Battery
Thermal throttling
Real networking
Vendor-specific Android behavior
```

Critical release testing needs physical devices.

---

# 134. Release Signing

Production mobile artifacts must be cryptographically signed.

Signing credentials are high-value production secrets.

They belong in controlled CI/release infrastructure—not developer repositories.

---

# 135. Android Signing Keys

Android signing keys require:

```text
Restricted access
Secure backup
Rotation/recovery planning
CI integration
Auditability
```

Loss or compromise can have severe release consequences.

---

# 136. iOS Signing

iOS certificates/profiles/App Store credentials require equivalent controlled management and automated renewal processes where practical.

---

# 137. Mobile CI/CD

Conceptually:

```text
Commit
  │
  ▼
Lint
  │
  ▼
Type Check
  │
  ▼
Unit / Component Tests
  │
  ▼
Security Scan
  │
  ▼
Build
  │
  ▼
Integration / E2E
  │
  ▼
Signed Artifact
  │
  ▼
Internal Testing
  │
  ▼
Store Release
```

---

# 138. Immutable Builds

The exact signed artifact approved for release should be traceable to:

```text
Source commit
Dependencies
Configuration
Build pipeline
Build number
Release
```

Rebuilding "the same version" later is not equivalent to preserving the original artifact.

---

# 139. Staged Rollout

New versions should use staged/phased rollout where supported.

```text
1%
 │
 ▼
5%
 │
 ▼
25%
 │
 ▼
50%
 │
 ▼
100%
```

Progression depends on health signals, not simply elapsed time.

---

# 140. Release Health Gates

Monitor:

```text
Crash-free sessions
ANRs/hangs
Startup failures
Authentication failures
API errors
Sync failures
Performance regression
```

A release with severe regressions should be halted before reaching all users.

---

# 141. Feature Flags

Feature flags can separate application deployment from feature activation.

```text
App Version
    │
    ▼
Feature Code Present
    │
    ▼
Remote Flag
    │
 ┌──┴──┐
 ▼     ▼
OFF    ON
```

Flags do not replace backend authorization.

---

# 142. Remote Configuration

Remote configuration may control safe operational values such as:

```text
Feature availability
UI configuration
Operational thresholds
Rollout percentages
```

It must not become a mechanism for remotely executing arbitrary code.

---

# 143. Minimum Supported Version

Backend systems should know which mobile versions remain supported.

```text
Current: 12.4
Minimum: 10.2
```

Versions below the minimum may receive an upgrade-required response where necessary.

---

# 144. Forced Upgrade

Forced upgrades should be rare.

Appropriate reasons may include:

```text
Critical security issue
Irreconcilable protocol incompatibility
Dangerously incorrect application behavior
```

Using forced updates for ordinary feature releases creates unnecessary user disruption.

---

# 145. API Compatibility Window

Because store approval and user adoption take time:

```text
Backend N
   │
   ├── Mobile N
   ├── Mobile N-1
   └── Older supported clients
```

must coexist.

Server teams cannot assume coordinated deployment with mobile clients.

---

# 146. OTA Updates

JavaScript/asset OTA updates may be useful where the chosen React Native/Expo architecture supports them.

But OTA updates must respect platform policies and native-runtime compatibility.

```text
JS Update
   │
   ▼
Compatible with installed native runtime?
   │
 ┌─┴─┐
 ▼   ▼
Yes  No
 │    │
OTA  Store binary required
```

---

# 147. Mobile Rollback

Rollback mechanisms depend on failure type.

```text
Feature problem
→ Disable flag

Compatible JS regression
→ OTA rollback where supported

Native binary regression
→ Halt rollout + submit corrected binary

Backend incompatibility
→ Restore compatibility server-side
```

There is no universal instant mobile rollback.

---

# 148. Mobile Anti-Patterns

Mediverse rejects:

```text
❌ Treating mobile as responsive web inside a wrapper
❌ Forcing 100% web/mobile code sharing
❌ Embedding OAuth client secrets in APK/IPA
❌ Collecting IdP passwords in arbitrary WebViews
❌ Storing refresh tokens in plaintext storage
❌ Biometrics treated as backend authorization
❌ Offline support implemented independently by screens
❌ In-memory-only queues for durable offline mutations
❌ Retryable mutations without idempotency
❌ Last-write-wins used blindly for user-generated content
❌ Full database download on every synchronization
❌ Ignoring remote deletions
❌ Assuming one user has one device
❌ Assuming background tasks always run
❌ Treating network connectivity indicator as API availability
❌ Push tokens treated as permanent user identity
❌ Sensitive information exposed on lock-screen notifications
❌ Push payload treated as authoritative state
❌ Redux used as a copy of the local database
❌ Unlimited query/image/media caches
❌ Desktop 3D assets shipped unchanged to phones
❌ Infinite socket reconnect loops
❌ Polling constantly while backgrounded
❌ Ignoring battery and cellular bandwidth
❌ Phone UI merely stretched onto tablets
❌ Secrets stored in application bundles
❌ Certificate pinning added without rotation planning
❌ Root detection treated as a security boundary
❌ WebViews with unrestricted navigation/bridges
❌ Requesting every permission on first launch
❌ Testing only on one emulator
❌ Testing offline features only with reliable Wi-Fi
❌ Testing only fresh database installations
❌ Signing keys committed to repositories
❌ Rebuilding production artifacts manually
❌ Releasing immediately to 100% of users
❌ Feature flags used as authorization
❌ Forced upgrades for ordinary releases
❌ Backend assuming every mobile client updates immediately
❌ OTA updates crossing incompatible native-runtime boundaries
```

---

# 149. Final Mediverse Mobile Reference Architecture

```text
                              USER
                               │
                               ▼
                 ┌─────────────────────────┐
                 │ MEDIVERSE MOBILE        │
                 │ React Native + TS       │
                 │ Android / iOS           │
                 └────────────┬────────────┘
                              │
       ┌──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┐
       ▼                      ▼                      ▼
      UI                  DOMAIN LAYER          DEVICE LAYER
       │                      │                      │
       │                      │             ┌────────┼────────┐
       │                      │             ▼        ▼        ▼
       │                      │          Secure    Push   Biometrics
       │                      │          Storage
       │                      │
       └──────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
                              ▼                               │
                         REPOSITORIES                         │
                              │                               │
                ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐                 │
                ▼                           ▼                 │
          LOCAL DATABASE                REMOTE API            │
                │                           │                 │
       ┌────────┼─────────┐                 │                 │
       ▼        ▼         ▼                 │                 │
   Metadata   Offline   Sync Queue           │                 │
             Content       │                 │                 │
                           ▼                 │                 │
                      SYNC ENGINE            │                 │
                           │                 │                 │
          ┌────────────────┼─────────────┐   │                 │
          ▼                ▼             ▼   │                 │
      Idempotency       Conflicts      Delta Sync              │
          │                │             │                     │
          └────────────────┼─────────────┘                     │
                           ▼                                   │
                      API CLIENT ◄─────────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
                       API GATEWAY
                           │
                           ▼
                   MEDIVERSE SERVICES
                           │
          ┌────────────────┼──────────────────┐
          ▼                ▼                  ▼
       DOMAIN           CONTENT          NOTIFICATION
       SERVICES         SERVICES            SERVICE
                                               │
                                      ┌────────┴────────┐
                                      ▼                 ▼
                                     FCM               APNs


              ───────── OFFLINE PLANE ─────────

     Downloads → Local DB → Filesystem → Sync Queue
          │                                  │
          └──────────────► Sync Engine ◄─────┘


              ───────── SECURITY PLANE ────────

       OAuth/OIDC + PKCE
              │
       Secure Token Storage
              │
       Device Security Signals
              │
       TLS / Input Validation
              │
       Backend Authorization


              ───────── QUALITY PLANE ─────────

     Unit → Component → Sync Tests → Integration
                         │
                         ▼
                    Mobile E2E
                         │
                         ▼
                   Device Matrix
                         │
                         ▼
            Offline / Upgrade Testing


              ───────── DELIVERY PLANE ────────

                       Source
                         │
                         ▼
                        CI
                         │
                         ▼
                    Signed Build
                         │
              ┌──────────┴──────────┐

              │                     │
```
